import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Group the data by 'intro.pathway' and calculate the mean mrt for each group
grouped_data = invasion_success.groupby('intro.pathway')['mrt'].mean()

# Perform an ANOVA to test for significant differences in mrt across introduction pathways
anova_result = f_oneway(*[invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == pathway]['mrt'] for pathway in grouped_data.index])

grouped_data, anova_result

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots', and 'invaded.niche.breadth'
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots', 'invaded.niche.breadth', 'intro.pathway'])

# Fit a linear model to examine the interaction between 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway' on 'number.of.invaded.plots'
model = ols('number.of.invaded.plots ~ mrt * C(intro.pathway)', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots', and 'invaded.niche.breadth'
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots', 'invaded.niche.breadth', 'intro.pathway'])

# Separate the data by introduction pathway
agri_forest = invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == 'AgriForest']
gardening = invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == 'Gardening']
unintentional = invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == 'Unintentional']

# Fit a linear model for each pathway to examine the relationship between mrt and number.of.invaded.plots
model_agri_forest = ols('number.of.invaded.plots ~ mrt', data=agri_forest).fit()
model_gardening = ols('number.of.invaded.plots ~ mrt', data=gardening).fit()
model_unintentional = ols('number.of.invaded.plots ~ mrt', data=unintentional).fit()

# Extract the coefficients and p-values
coefficients = {
    'AgriForest': model_agri_forest.params['mrt'],
    'Gardening': model_gardening.params['mrt'],
    'Unintentional': model_unintentional.params['mrt']
}

p_values = {
    'AgriForest': model_agri_forest.pvalues['mrt'],
    'Gardening': model_gardening.pvalues['mrt'],
    'Unintentional': model_unintentional.pvalues['mrt']
}

coefficients, p_values

import pandas as pd

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots', and 'intro.pathway'
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots', 'intro.pathway'])

# Calculate the correlation coefficients between mrt and number.of.invaded.plots for each introduction pathway
correlation_agri_forest = invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == 'AgriForest'][['mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots']].corr().iloc[0, 1]
correlation_gardening = invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == 'Gardening'][['mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots']].corr().iloc[0, 1]
correlation_unintentional = invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == 'Unintentional'][['mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots']].corr().iloc[0, 1]

correlation_agri_forest, correlation_gardening, correlation_unintentional
